newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition fails to agree defence cuts.
newsitem.headline: German coalition fails to agree defence cuts.

text.p: Leaders of Germany's centre-right coalition on Tuesday failed to reach a decision on the future of the Eurofighter combat jet and around 200 million marks ($133.4 million) in defence spending cuts, coalition sources said.
Further talks on defence spending are expected, although a decision on placing a firm order to enable serial production of Eurofighter to begin may not now be taken this year.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has called for the defence cuts, which he maintains will not prevent Germany from joining Britain, Italy and Spain in funding the Eurofighter project.
The Free Democrats (FDP), the coalition's junior partner, have expressed strong doubts that Bonn will be able to reduce military spending and order its planned 180 Eurofighters at the same time.

Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), has said his ministry faced difficulties due to Bonn's effort to meet tight spending limits required for European economic and monetary union.

Ruehe has also said he would like to secure financing for the Eurofighter in the interest of the companies developing the plane. The government would have to raise 100 million marks from its 1997 budget for the jet's production.
Ruehe and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, an FDP member, took part in the coalition talks.
The Eurofighter, in which more than 6.5 billion marks have been invested since 1985, is needed to replace Germany's force of 40-year-old Phantom jets.
British Aerospace holds a 37.5 percent share of the project, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) 30 percent, Italy's Alenia 19.5 percent and Spain's Casa 13 percent.
The 200 million marks in defence cuts are part of an agreement the coalition reached at the weekend to cut spending by three billion marks next year to make up for a shortfall in tax revenues.
